Please solve this issue: Customers paste amounts like `"$1,234.50"` or `" 12 "` into the billing portal. Add `parse_amount(text)` to `ledgerly/importers.py` that turns such text into an amount: ignore surrounding whitespace, an optional leading `$` and thousands separators. Reject text that is not a valid non-negative amount with at most two decimal places.

## Notes from earlier work
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Reject invalid billing input by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with codes like `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity`, `negative_amount`, matching the existing `issue_invoice` pattern.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-c0024] Customer-entered amount detail: In the customer-entered amount export the CSV columns are separated by semicolons for the finance spreadsheet.
  (learned from task T4024 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-c0038] Customer-entered amount detail: The customer-entered amount feature flag is read from settings.FEATURES at import time.
  (learned from task T4038 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-c0044] Customer-entered amount detail: In tests for customer-entered amount, the fixture customer cus_test_200 already has one draft entry.
  (learned from task T4044 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0007] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Per finance policy FIN-2026-03, support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when the amount exceeds the threshold and no approver is given. Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary Decimal results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 3x, 2 passed, 1 failed)
